messages.subject: Calculating coverage of genomic regions
messages.body_plain:
I am interested to know if methylkit can be used to find out the coverage of specific regions in the genome. For example of all the potential enhancers or promoters rich in CpGs in a reference genome (example annotated promoters or enhancers in mouse genome)  how many of them are actually well covered through the ERRBS sequencing
If this is not possible through methylkit any recommendations on how to do this using the ERRBS data?

Thank you,
Linda

messages.body_plain:
Hi Britta,

You were right, this is a bug if input is a methylBaseDB, I will follow up on this!

In our latest documentation on bioconductor you can find descriptions of the functions you required to subset your data (here <https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#52_converting_methylkit_objects_to_methyldb_objects_and_vice_versa>).
So in general we do not provide a direct way to subset a DB into a smaller DB (to avoid writing to many files),
so the subset will be a normal (nonDB) object. But what you can do is to use the function makeMethylDB(),
which can create the methylDB pendant for your corresponding input object.

Same holds for the simulation, you can use makeMethylDB() on the result of the dataSim() function, which can simulate the data for a methylBase object.

If you have any further questions, or need more details please ask!

Best Alex
